skill.name: writing-great-skills
skill.description: Reference for writing and editing predictable AI skills with clear invocation, structure, and pruning rules.
skill.summary: Guides authors in writing predictable, lean, and well-structured AI skills.

content.value_statement: AI skills can become hard to invoke, maintain, and trust. This skill gives authors a vocabulary for predictable skill design.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use model-invoked skills and user-invoked skills.
Defines how to write short descriptions with clear trigger branches.
Describes information hierarchy for steps, inline reference, and disclosed reference.
Shows how progressive disclosure keeps SKILL.md focused and readable.
Names failure modes such as duplication, sprawl, sediment, no-op text, and negation.
Provides a glossary of shared terms for reviewing and improving skill drafts.
limitations: It is a reference skill, not an automated validator.
It does not generate complete skill packages by itself.
It does not test model behavior across real agent runs.
It focuses on writing quality, not runtime security controls.

use_cases.title: Review a Draft Skill
use_cases.description: Evaluate a draft for invocation clarity, duplicated meaning, weak completion criteria, and misplaced reference material.

use_cases.title: Design a Skill Library
use_cases.description: Decide which skills should be model-invoked, user-invoked, split, merged, or connected through a router skill.

use_cases.title: Create Shared Review Language
use_cases.description: Use consistent terms for discussions about context load, cognitive load, progressive disclosure, and predictable agent behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Check Invocation Choice
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill draft. Tell me whether it should be model-invoked or user-invoked, and explain the tradeoff.

prompt_templates.title: Prune a Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this skill description. Keep only distinct trigger branches, remove duplicate wording, and preserve the leading words.

prompt_templates.title: Reorganize Skill Content
prompt_templates.scenario: Move material into the right level of the information hierarchy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SKILL.md structure. Identify steps, inline reference, disclosed reference, and material that should move.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Failure Modes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a mature skill or skill set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these skills for premature completion, duplication, sediment, sprawl, no-op text, and negation. Recommend exact edits.

output_examples.input: A skill has a long description with three similar trigger phrases.
output_examples.output: The review identifies one real branch, removes duplicate trigger wording, and keeps one clear leading word for invocation.

output_examples.input: A SKILL.md file mixes steps, definitions, and long background sections.
output_examples.output: The review separates ordered steps from reference material and recommends which definitions should move behind a context pointer.

output_examples.input: A team is unsure whether to split one large skill into smaller skills.
output_examples.output: The review compares context load, cognitive load, independent invocation needs, and premature completion risk before recommending a split.

best_practices: Use model invocation only when the agent or another skill must discover the skill.
Keep each meaning in one authoritative place to reduce drift and maintenance cost.
Move branch-specific reference into linked files when every run does not need it.
anti_patterns: Do not repeat the same trigger branch with several synonyms.
Do not keep stale background text because it feels safer than deleting it.
Do not steer behavior mainly by describing what the agent should avoid.

faq.question: What does this skill help me write?
faq.answer: It helps you write AI skills with clearer invocation, stronger structure, and less unnecessary text.

faq.question: Does it run any tools or commands?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation and reference material for authors and reviewers.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude Code and Codex skills?
faq.answer: Yes. The concepts apply to Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and similar agent skill systems.

faq.question: What is progressive disclosure?
faq.answer: It means moving reference material out of SKILL.md when only some branches need it.

faq.question: When should I split a skill?
faq.answer: Split a skill when independent invocation or hidden later steps improve predictable behavior enough to justify the added load.

faq.question: Is this a security auditing skill?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on writing quality, structure, invocation, and maintainability.
